content:
Harish Reddy: heads up: staging pilot pool expand is failing at `terraform apply` 😬

Error looks like IAM-ish + quota-ish (two different runs). Dropping logs below. Anyone on point?

```
module.dedicated_pool.aws_eks_node_group.gpu: Creating...
╷
│ Error: error creating EKS Node Group (ded-pool-stg-usw2-gpu-ng): AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::***:assumed-role/fleet-provisioner-stg/i-0c3... is not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::***:role/eks-node-instance-role-stg
│ status code: 403, request id: 2f5b...
╵

...and another run:

╷
│ Error: creating EC2 Launch Template: MaxSpotInstanceCountExceeded: You have requested more Spot instances (4) than your current Spot instance limit (0).
│ status code: 400, request id: 0b19...
╵
```

Gabe Wilson: thanks. two separate failure modes. first one is definitely missing `iam:PassRole` on the provisioner role.

Can you paste the run link / correlation id from the provisioner output?

Harish Reddy: correlation id `provrun_01HQ9TQ6WJ3QZ6H1C2Y9K2E9M7` (from CLI). also terraform stderr is in the run artifact.

Vanessa Ortiz: ack. @Gabe Wilson can you open an INT for the IAM permission? We should not be patching ad hoc in console.

Also: quota error looks like staging is trying to use Spot by default (?) which we probably shouldn’t for pilot.

Nina Petrova: +1. For staging pilot we can force on-demand to unblock, but let’s keep it consistent with prod module defaults.

Question: is this pool using `capacity_type = SPOT` from the module, or did the wrapper set it?

terraform-bot: apply failed (exit 1) for workspace `ded-pool-stg-usw2` on commit `c4d91a2`.

Keiko Yamamoto: I can check module variables. In `redwood-terraform` we added regional defaults last week; I think staging has `use_spot=true` in `env/staging.tfvars`.

If the account spot limit is 0, any spot request will fail even if the rest is fine.

Sahana Iyer: re retry: for the IAM error, rerunning won’t help until policy is fixed.

For quota/spot error: rerun will keep failing unless we flip to on-demand or request spot limit increase.

Gabe Wilson: created INT ticket for IAM passrole: INT-1044 (staging provisioner role missing PassRole for node instance role). Linking here: https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/INT-1044

I’ll push a small change to the staging provisioner policy once we confirm exact role ARN patterns.

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: thanks. Can we also add a guardrail in the orchestrator to detect this and produce a nicer message? (actionable: “missing iam:PassRole on X”).

Harish Reddy: what do you want me to do short-term to keep pilot moving? We’re blocked on the pool expansion window.

Nina Petrova: short-term unblock for spot:
- set `capacity_type = ON_DEMAND` / `use_spot=false` for staging pilot pool
- re-run `terraform apply`

But: only do this if we’re confident the pilot doesn’t need spot semantics.

Keiko Yamamoto: agree. for pilot readiness gates we just need nodes up; spot isn’t required.

If we flip to on-demand, we also avoid churn during validation.

Victor Alvarez: quick note: if we reprovision nodes, make sure the SG rules still include the DNS/TLS checks. last time we had missing egress in staging. (don’t want to chase two failures at once)

Gabe Wilson: retry guidance (so we’re consistent):

1) IAM AccessDenied (PassRole): do NOT retry blindly. Fix policy, then re-run from Provisioning stage.
2) Quota / Spot limit: either request quota increase or change config to not request Spot. Retrying won’t fix.

For right now, set staging to on-demand and re-run.

Command:
`rw fleet provision --pool ded-pool-stg-usw2 --rerun-stage provisioning --dry-run=false`

Harish Reddy: ok flipping staging tfvars now (use_spot=false). will re-run via CLI.

Vanessa Ortiz: please post the diff in thread + tag @Keiko Yamamoto for sanity.

Harish Reddy: diff:

```
# env/staging.tfvars
-use_spot = true
+use_spot = false
```

Re-running now.

terraform-bot: apply in progress for workspace `ded-pool-stg-usw2`…

Keiko Yamamoto: looks good for pilot. Longer term we should (a) set a sane default per env and (b) surface the account quota/limits in the preflight checks.

Sahana Iyer: +1 preflight. We can add a lightweight “quota check” step before apply (even if best-effort) and fail fast with a clear message.

Gabe Wilson: update: INT-1044 assigned to me. I’m adding explicit PassRole for `eks-node-instance-role-*` in staging policy (scoped to account + prefix). Will also add a unit test in policy generation.

Vanessa Ortiz: thanks. Let’s capture follow-up in Linear as well but for now: unblock pilot.

Harish Reddy: apply succeeded after turning off spot 🎉

Now hitting next stage (bootstrap). Will keep you posted if any more infra side issues.

Victor Alvarez: :eyes: if bootstrap fails, paste the error + run id. also make sure new nodes can reach artifact mirror.

Vanessa Ortiz: closing the loop: root cause summary so far:
- IAM: missing `iam:PassRole` (tracked in INT-1044)
- Quota: staging spot limit = 0; mitigated by forcing on-demand

We should add both to the “failure mode inventory” doc for week 1/2.

Gabe Wilson: :thumbsup: I’ll link this thread in the INT and in the runbook once the policy fix lands.
